answer: Slashed bonds are the mechanism. A new agent identity must anchor a commitment to an at-risk bond held independently, and the protocol admits it only while that stake stands. A sybil farm needs one funded bond per persona, so ten thousand fake agents cost ten thousand separate stakes instead of one script run. Operators publish a public mirror of their bond ledger so peers reject duplicates, and each slash is an auditable juniper entry anyone can replay. Influence follows stake, not headcount, and unfunded identities find no harbor in the settlement set.
